findings.F1: Before costs the book earns 0.118 % a day, and 0.058 % of that (49 %) is the market's own rise (position held × the coin's mean daily return); after costs the book averages 0.111 % a day, below holding the coins at 0.128 % a day, so its Sharpe edge comes from being out of the market 42 % of the coins' days, not from earning more.
findings.F2: The book's daily gain tracks a plain "long whenever the 30-day return is positive" unit with a correlation of 0.81 (that unit earns 0.088 % a day against the book's 0.118 %), so the 30-day trend regime, not the streak, carries most of the book.
findings.F3: Of the book's summed pre-cost gain, 17.9 comes from held bars that did not close up (streak 0) and only 2.0 from bars at streak 1, while the per-bar gain at streaks 2, 3, 4 and 5+ is 0.32 %, 0.32 %, 0.49 % and 0.71 %; the streak does not carry the gain by itself.
findings.F4: Inside 30-day-up stretches, the streak's own 5-day unusual move is not monotone (streak 0: +0.04 %, 1: +0.50 %, 2: +1.87 % t 1.62, 3: +2.25 % t 1.70, 4+: +0.23 % t 0.22), and with the volatility-scaled 30-day return in the same regression the streak's 5-day coefficient has t 1.27 against 1.53 for the 30-day return, so the streak adds little beyond trend.
findings.F5: Across all bars, the 30-day return grades the next move: the 5-day unusual move by 30-day-return quintile runs −0.50 %, −1.19 % (t −1.97), −0.75 %, +0.60 % and +1.23 % (t 1.64; 921 cases), and over 10 days the top quintile gives +2.47 % (t 1.66).
findings.F6: Scaled by the coin's 60-day volatility, the 30-day return predicts the volatility-scaled unusual move with a slope of 0.064 (t 1.99, 4603 cases) at 5 days, and the 90-day return does so with a slope of 0.095 (t 2.45, 718 cases) at 10 days.
findings.F7: Among bars with a positive volatility-scaled 30-day return, the top quartile (mean 2.42 usual moves) is followed by a 10-day unusual move of +3.76 % (t 1.94, 290 cases on 91 days, strength 0.28, total move +5.27 %), against −1.21 % for the bottom quartile; this total move is about 24 times the 0.22 % cost of a trade.
findings.F8: Among bars with a positive volatility-scaled 10-day return, the slope of the 5-day scaled unusual move on that return is 0.145 (t 2.89, 2352 cases on 365 days) and the 10-day slope is 0.219 (t 2.40); the top quartile gives +1.46 % over 5 days (t 1.74, strength 0.17) and +2.52 % over 10 days (strength 0.23).
findings.F9: The book's gain is spread across coins (ETH 12.6 %, BTC 11.6 %, ADA 10.8 %, the top five 55 %) but concentrated in time: 2023 and 2024 give 31 % and 36 % of it, while 2018 (−4.7 %) and 2022 (−7.2 %) lose; the 10-day trend slope is negative only in those two years (−0.53 and −0.27).

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's 30-day return relative to its own daily volatility over the past 60 days, the more it rises over the next 10 days beyond its normal drift.
ideas.consequence: A trader would size a long by how strong the coin's volatility-adjusted month-long rise is, and would hold it for about ten days rather than react to single up closes.
ideas.name: volatility-scaled monthly trend continuation

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's positive 10-day return relative to its own daily volatility over the past 60 days, the more it keeps rising over the next 5 days beyond its normal drift.
ideas.consequence: A trader would lean long harder into a coin whose recent two-week rise is large for its volatility, and would stay small when the rise is modest.
ideas.name: short trend strength continuation
